title: Effects of nectar robbing on nectar dynamics and bumblebee foraging strategies in Linaria vulgaris (Scrophulariaceae)
orientation_basis: shorter proboscis relative to nectar-spur access -> greater switching to secondary robbing; longer-tongued bees are less likely to switch
evidence_basis: Primary field study explicitly asks whether shorter-tongued bumblebees are most likely to become secondary robbers and reports that longer-tongued bees were less likely to switch even when nearly all flowers had been pierced.
notes: Eligibility was frozen direction-blind in source eligibility Batch7.
